title: Automated In-Situ Mechanical Testing to Enhance Data-Driven Analysis of Additively Manufactured 316L Stainless Steel
content: Additive manufacturing (AM) has made possible many interesting component designs and enabled complex topological optimization [1]. Metal AM has also introduced an equally complex microstructural landscape which is based on material, method, and print parameters [2]. One example of the unique microstructural considerations is dislocation cell generation in AM metals, like austenitic stainless steel, which are primarily produced by the constrained thermal expansion/contraction cycles during printing [3]. This variability makes the properties of such materials more difficult to predict than standard wrought or cast components. Because of this, adoption of AM components is somewhat more tenuous than traditionally manufactured components, and part-specific quality control can be more challenging.
